title: Working at Werlein's and joining the school board
summary: He tells of the Buescher cornet he tried at Werlein's while playing with Earl Crumb, and of his later years with the school board.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: about to say in the series robot catalog around 1910 I thought I remembered but I'm not quite sure whether it was in that catalog or later I do remember the first time I saw a trumpet in series robot catalog and I remember thinking how ugly it looked it looked like a bugle you know stretched out cornet and I thought it was ugly and I still think it's ugly I think a beautifully made cornet is much prettier than a trumpet and of course I like the sound of it too it goes without saying so I always had a cornet along with me when I played in the big bands did you have a shank did you use the same mouthpiece I use the trumpet mouthpiece I cut out on a lathe myself to fit my I cut it down sort of lopsided it wasn't such a good fit but anyway I did fit in both arms oh no no I you see I had two vega mouthpieces. And one of them I cut down short to fit on a trumpet, on a cornet. And the other one I let alone. Well, they were both the same thing, you see. So I just pick up the mouthpiece and the cornet all at once when it came time for me to take a solo. And I remember when I was playing with Earl Crumbs out of suburban gardens, I got a hold of a busher cornet. Why they ever stopped making that thing, I don't know, because it had a great big beautiful tone. It was a lovely thing, but they had rigged up the tubes in it so you couldn't get your right thumb any place. The right thumb was dangling in space. There was no, you know how you put your right thumb under the tube which leads to the mouthpiece and you can put it around the valves too if you want. There was no place for your thumb to go on that doggone thing. And it was very uncomfortable to get used to in the beginning. See, after I got used to it, it was perfectly alright. But gee, I'll never forget, imagine Busher, I never did have much respect for the Busher. Am I saying something wrong? No. I'm not on television. I'm not on radio. Well anyway, I never did have much respect for the Busher manufacturing company and I don't believe many other people did as a musical manufacturer. But anyway, boy, they put out a really fine cornet and they took it off of the market. I'd sure like to be able to run across one of those things. Well, I was working at Whirlions then and I
was playing with Earl Crum at the same time. What years did you work with them? Can you remember

about that? Whirlions? Yeah. Let me see. In the twenties, huh? Betty. Betty. She's gone up. Oh yeah, it was very late. It was very late in the twenties though. Just about as late as you could. It may have been in the... Well, the best I can do is say it was in the very late twenties. When you worked
there, was it just as a clerk or were you connected with the music school or what? No, no. I was...

When I worked there at one time, I was a clerk at this time that I'm talking about. Later on I went back and I had charge of the music school. Yeah, that's where I'm talking. But at this time I was selling instruments in the band instrument behind the counter. And they couldn't sell the thing. It just stayed there. Nobody wanted it. They'd take it to blow on, they couldn't get their thumb anyway. So they'd give it back in discouragement. So I took it out there to try it out to see what it sounded like. And oh boy, it was marvelous. It was marvelous. A real marvelous song. It had such a great big bore and such a great big sound. I just enjoyed playing that thing. It's too bad I didn't buy it. I could have bought it for under wholesale price, I'm quite sure. I guess they finally sold it on a sale. I most likely had left Well Eyes by that time and gone with the school board teaching. When did you go with the school? Do you remember? Well, that's what I say. I think I went with the school board in... Batty?
You cooked to 1930 according to... 1930 or 1931. Let me see. It should have been 17 years and then 15 before that or something.

30, 40, 50, 60. It must have been 30 because I was with... I retired after having been with them almost 30 years. I think I got credit for being with them 30 years because they... Yeah, it was about two years ago. They give you some... Yeah. So it's 62 now. I retired about two years ago or maybe a little bit before that but I think they gave me credit for 30 years. You can retire after 30 years or you can retire after 60. So I was 60 then. So I could...
